The test image shows a tomato **leaf** with severe necrosis — large brown/tan dried areas with holes (tissue falling out), yellowing at margins, papery texture. The leaf part narrows candidates to 12 leaf-affecting classes.

Now I'll view reference images one at a time, starting with the most likely candidates based on the visual pattern.

**Summary of visual analysis:**

- **Test image**: Severely necrotic tomato leaf, mostly brown/tan papery tissue, multiple round holes/perforations, yellow border, placed on white surface
- **Late_Blight**: Large brown papery area — some similarity but no holes
- **TSWV**: Ring patterns on mostly green leaf — not similar
- **Early_Blight**: Small dark lesion with concentric rings on green leaf — not similar
- **Septoria**: Small circular spots on green leaf — not similar
- **Verticillium_Wilt (LeafNet_265)**: **BEST MATCH** — large brown irregular necrosis with yellow halo, round holes in tissue, white background setting — highly similar
- **Verticillium_Wilt (LeafNet_317)**: Also similar brown/yellow necrosis pattern
- **Gray_Mold**: Brown blotches from margin — somewhat similar but no holes
- **Phytophthora_Blight**: Water-soaked slimy large brown area — not matching the dry papery texture

The Verticillium Wilt references (particularly LeafNet_265) match the test image most closely: large brown/yellow necrotic V-shaped lesion, round perforations in the leaf tissue, and similar white-surface examination setting.
